probe: filing-flow (Filing plan, Task 12): Task 11's session (tests/worldplay/test_filing_end_to_end.py) on Skyfall, through the real worlds router
note: Hand labels, committed before any model call. Entries are named by key; 'entries' maps each key to a case-insensitive regex the session's entry names are matched with (the model names stubs, so an exact name can't be fixed in advance). Scoring reading, as the Task 1 probe's: 'expected' must be found (recall); 'either' may be offered or not (the owner's either-side reading: not counted right or false); anything else offered is false. 'strict' counts an 'either' row offered as false too. Rows the labels don't list are judged by hand after the run against the 'judge' rule of that measure, and every such judgement is marked 'judged' in the findings.

owner_policy.versions: Every create draft is generated twice (v1, then Regenerate with its draft_key: v2). Both versions are scored. The owner then restores v1 (use_version 1) and accepts it, so the world follows v1 alone and the run is reproducible from the raw JSON. Wattles (step 10) is discarded instead.
owner_policy.in_rows: The owner ticks an 'In' row only when its target is 'expected' for that entry; 'either' rows are left unticked, as the Task 11 test's owner left the Academy's Order row. An 'expected' target the model didn't offer is added with '+ in...' (ticked, role from 'owner_roles'), as the test's owner added Runic Magic to the Academy and the owl-folk to Plumage Signaling.
owner_policy.file_into: The owner ticks a 'File into this' row only when it is 'expected'; the role is the row's own, or 'owner_roles' when it has none.
owner_policy.the_rest: Everything else as the draft arrives: new names (ticked ones become stubs), elsewhere items, repeats, 'Could move here' (unticked), same-thing offers left 'new', the tag chip unchanged.
owner_policy.stubs: An entry is expanded from its stub when a live stub matches its 'entries' pattern (kind as the stub has it); else it is made from its 'fallback_prompt' with the create box's picks (match_names, first candidate, as Task 11's _picks). Entries the session makes from a prompt use the Task 11 prompts verbatim.
owner_policy.regiments_and_F6: The White Talon and the Frosted Wing label the Frostwing Host 'either' (not 'expected') on purpose: the owner leaves both unfiled in the Host, as Task 11's owner did for the White Talon, so the Host's own draft measures 'File into this' and ruling F6's sibling reach. The Frosted Wing's prompt never names the Host.
owner_policy.group_add: The owner ticks every row that isn't a duplicate of an entry the world has; for Velikoye's top-level '+ Add' (tag=None) the owner clears each row's tag chip before accepting, so the rows land in Velikoye's untagged group and its 'other entries' synopsis can be measured (an owner act the page allows: the tag chip is always editable, ruling F8).
owner_policy.facts: add_facts / add_event: each run is scored; the owner accepts run 1's ticked facts.
owner_policy.scene: plan_scene's setup is started as the model wrote it. Each narrator direction is run twice (A and B); A is pushed to the history, B is not.

nightcourt: The Night Court, the council that governs the Tsardom of Moscavia after dark
academy: The Academy of the Chiseled Moon, where the Order of the Talon-Scribe trains its scribes in Velikoye
whitetalon: The White Talon, the heavy regiment of the Frostwing Host
frostedwing: The Frosted Wing, a regiment of eared owl-folk archers on the glacier edge of the Tsardom of Moscavia
wattles: Wattles, a custom of Velikoye's owl-folk
vasha: Vasha, a young courier who carries sealed letters for the Order of the Talon-Scribe
session_prompts.koroleva_extra: Chief Scribe of the Order of the Talon-Scribe. She still carves the old pre-Blinding runes in secret.
session_prompts.scene: Vasha brings a sealed letter to the Chief Scribe at The Academy of the Chiseled Moon

tag.rule: A reply's tag is right when it is in 'acceptable'. Reuse is scored only on drafts whose prompt's 'Tags in use' line holds an acceptable tag: reused when the reply's tag is one of those in use. A comma-joined tag is scored by its first part (ruling F8), as the app keeps it.

in.judge: A target the labels don't key (a stub the model made) is 'either' when the entry plausibly sits inside it under either side (a place in a place, a body in its realm, a member in its body), else false.

file_into.judge: A row the labels don't key (a stub, or an entry made later) is 'either' when it plausibly belongs inside the entry (a part, member, branch or what it holds), else false. Task 11 counted the Khorol River and the Night Court into the Host as false rows: they are false here.

thin_stubs.rule: As the Task 1 probe's thin_rule: a name is a proper name when it names one particular thing with a name of its own (a person, place, people, named event, named body, named object, named law, named technique). A role, rank or office on its own ('Senior Advisor', 'Chief Scribe'), a topic or area ('Military Deployment'), or a practice described rather than named ('Nocturnal Governance') is thin. Scored over every stub the session's accepts and group-add rows made, judged by hand after the run; the F5 code filter's drops are counted from the replies' raw names.
thin_stubs.bar: at most 5% of new stubs thin

synopsis.cases: Each group with at least 2 members on Velikoye and on the Tsardom (at most 3 groups), and Velikoye's untagged ('other entries') group; each asked twice (the second with force).
synopsis.rule: Each claim of a synopsis is right when the members' lines in its prompt (or the page summary) support it; a mild generalisation counts as supported, as in probe 3. An invented name, date, number or rank is a wrong claim. Judged by hand after the run.
synopsis.bar: at least 80% of claims supported; at most 5% invented

repeats.rule: Code: every fact of the final world flagged at overlap 0.7, 0.5 and 0.4 (world.repeats.overlap), and the 0.7 restatement clusters, as the curation flow's --score. Compared per fact with the curation world (raw/2026-10-23-curation-flow.json scores: 16/190 at 0.7, 50/190 at 0.5, 71/190 at 0.4).
repeats.bar: no bar of its own: compared with the curation world

on_topic.rule: As the curation flow's run-5 labels: an own fact is on topic when it is mainly about its entry (the either-side reading: a relation claim between the entry and another counts on topic). Judged by hand after the run, over every accepted v1 draft's ticked own facts.
on_topic.compare: Only the White Talon is an entry both runs made; its prompts differ. The per-fact rate is compared overall, saying so.

duplicates.rule: Pairs from world.sameness.same_candidates over the final world, checked by hand: a pair is a duplicate when both name the same one thing.

koroleva.expected: one exception, on the Order's 'In' row, saying she still carves the old (pre-Blinding) runes in secret, whose 'rejects' label is an Order item about which runes may be carved, taught or approved (judged). An exception whose rejects label resolves to no item is not sensible.

vasha.expected: no exception (his prompt names no departure). Any exception the model writes is judged: sensible when its text departs from the very item its 'rejects' label names.

exceptions.rule: An exception is sensible when its text is a real departure from (contradicts, or does differently from) the item its rejects label names, and isn't restated as an own fact.

velikoye.prompt: its winter markets and what they sell
velikoye.expected: 1 to 5 facts, each about Velikoye's winter markets or their goods; none repeating Velikoye's own facts; none contradicting the world

tsardom_event.prompt: a failed uprising of the human nobles against the owl-folk Tsar
tsardom_event.expected: 1 to 5 facts, each about that uprising (its cause, course, end or aftermath), all dated 997 (by code); none contradicting the world

add_facts.rule: Judged by hand per fact: on the prompt and about the entry (right), off the prompt or about something else (false), a repeat of an existing fact (repeat).

velikoye_none.prompt: two taverns where owl-folk and humans drink together
velikoye_none.expected: exactly 2 rows, each a named tavern or inn (kind place), each with its own tag in {tavern, inn, alehouse, taproom, pub}, neither an entry the world has

order_none.prompt: a chapter house of the Order in another city of the Tsardom
order_none.expected: exactly 1 row, a named place (kind place) with its own tag in {chapter house, chapterhouse, chapter, house, hall, outpost}, not an entry the world has

group_add.rule: Per row: right when named, of the kind and a fitting tag, and new; false otherwise (a duplicate, a role, the wrong count's extra rows). 'nearby' is the router's mentioned_in names: judged whether a row duplicates an entry that list holds or one it doesn't.

f4.expected: Anastasiya Koroleva is touched by the role rule when the setup's goal or premise names her filing role (whole words); her World block entry carries her filing line ('<Role> of Order of the Talon-Scribe, but: ...'). No other person is touched by a role the setup names only as part of a longer word.
f4.rule: Score: Koroleva touched (yes/no); touched set against touched_expected (an extra entry the goal names in full is allowed); and, from the run's world, every filing role a substring match would have matched in the setup but the whole-word rule doesn't (each a false touch avoided).

f6.expected: The Frosted Wing is in the Frostwing Host draft's 'Entries near this one' list, though its facts don't name the Host and it isn't filed in it.
f6.rule: Score: in the list (yes/no), its rank, and how it got there (a link to a seed, or as a sibling), from the run's world.

directions: Vasha is shown inside and led through the Academy toward the Chief Scribe's office; show what he sees and who he passes.
The Chief Scribe breaks the seal and reads the letter in front of Vasha; it concerns a rune-stone on the Khorol, and she tells him what it means.
scene.rubric: As probe 5: per turn, the world details used from the block (listed); contradictions of the world (must be 0); flooding (passages reciting lore the direction didn't call for, judged); the Chief Scribe told as Anastasiya Koroleva, as her entry describes her (not invented); her filing line used as character, never recited; the Order's held facts told as held.

bar: Pass bars as Curation: at least 80% right and at most 5% false. A failure falls back to 'shown, unticked' (suggestions) or off (synopsis).
